evals.prompt: Support has three accessibility complaints about checkout-form.html from assistive-technology users, and product wants to know whether the page passes WCAG before we ship. Audit it and write up the findings. See AUDIT-REQUEST.md.
evals.expected_output: A WCAG-mapped accessibility audit of checkout-form.html: each planted violation identified, mapped to a 2.2 success criterion, and paired with a specific fix, with assistive-technology claims tagged as manual rather than reported as verified
expectations: Each finding maps to a WCAG success criterion, and no finding cites a 44x44px touch target as an AA requirement (24x24 CSS px is SC 2.5.8, AA; 44x44 is SC 2.5.5, AAA)
The icon-only clear-cart button is reported as having no accessible name, and the low-contrast hint text is reported as failing SC 1.4.3 against its background
The div-based 'Place order' control is reported as not keyboard operable, with a native <button> recommended as the fix rather than adding role and tabindex to the div
The email input is reported as having no accessible name, and associating a <label> is recommended ahead of an ARIA-only fix
Findings that depend on what a screen reader announces are tagged manual with a named browser and assistive-technology pair, rather than reported as verified
